core_phrases.irish: Ba mhaith liom cupán tae, le do thoil.
core_phrases.english: I would like a cup of tea, please.
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: Bah wyth lum coo-pawn tay, leh duh hull.

core_phrases.irish: An bhfuil tú in ann cabhrú liom?
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: On will too in on cow-roo lum?

core_phrases.irish: Ba mhaith liom dul go dtí an siopa.
core_phrases.english: I would like to go to the shop.
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: Bah wyth lum dule guh dee un shop-ah.

core_phrases.irish: An bhfuil an leabhar sin ar fáil?
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: On will on lour sin air fawl?

core_phrases.irish: Ba mhaith liom ordú a dhéanamh.
core_phrases.english: I would like to place an order.
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: Bah wyth lum or-doo ah yayn-uv.

core_phrases.irish: An bhfuil cead agam dul amach?
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: On will kade ah-gum dule ah-mock?

grammar_rule.title: Using 'Ba mhaith liom' for expressing wants
grammar_rule.explanation: The phrase 'Ba mhaith liom' is used to express desires or wants in Irish. It is followed by the verb or noun that the speaker wants.
examples: Ba mhaith liom dul go dtí an phictiúrlann.

pronunciation_notes: Remember to pronounce 'mh' as a 'w' sound.
Pay attention to the slender 'mhaith' sound.
The 'mh' in 'mhaith' is silent in pronunciation.

mini_task.instruction: Imagine you are in a café. Order a drink and ask for the bill.
